🛡️ Official Singapore Wage Verification & Provenance Audit

Full empirical transparency: Audited breakdown of reported official figures vs. statutory benchmarks vs. actuarially imputed and calibrated roles.

Source: MOM OWS 2024 & Public Statutes
🟢 1. MOM Survey Reported 535 Codes (53.2%)

Directly reported by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) in the Occupational Wage Survey (OWS) 2024 published on Data.gov.sg (resource d_9917e751f7498502f70052a940a3f312).

Covers private commercial establishments with ≥25 employees where resident sample size is statistically significant (≥10 respondents). Contains verified 25th, 50th, and 75th percentile basic and gross wages.
🏛️ 2. Statutory / Gazetted 42 Apex Roles

Governed by official Singapore Parliamentary Statutes & Gazetted Frameworks, not surveyed in private commercial employer wage surveys.

Includes Prime Minister (S$110k/mo base, S$2.2M benchmark), Cabinet Ministers (MR4 benchmark: S$55k/mo base + 7mo bonus), Members of Parliament (S$192,500/yr allowance = S$16,041/mo), Judges, and Senior Civil Servants.
🟡 3. Actuarially Imputed & Calibrated 468 Codes (46.5%)

Statistical models for niche occupations suppressed by MOM (sample size <10) and sub-title seniority multipliers within broad 5-digit occupational baskets.

Triangulates SingStat TableBuilder Series M182171, 2-digit Sub-Major group regressions, and empirical market multipliers across C-Suite (1.70x), Directors (1.30x), Managers (1.05x), and Juniors (0.85x).

🔍 Why do different job titles under the same SSOC code have different market compensation?

Official statistical classifications like SSOC 2024 group many related job titles under a single 5-digit occupational code (e.g., SSOC 11110 encompasses Cabinet Minister, Attorney General, and Legislator / Member of Parliament; SSOC 12111 encompasses Chief Financial Officer, Finance Director, and Assistant Finance Manager). MOM publishes survey data only at the 5-digit code level and never at the individual sub-title level.

In real Singapore corporate and public sector practice, an apex Cabinet Minister or Chief Financial Officer earns substantially more than a backbench MP or Assistant Manager. The Singapore Career Actuarial Engine resolves this disparity by applying Statutory Gazetted Benchmarks to public roles and Actuarial Seniority Multipliers to private roles, ensuring every single one of the 9,449 titles reflects its true market compensation.
